hook.text: "If pigs fly, I'll give you a million dollars." Pigs don't fly. Is my promise broken? Formally: no.

buildup.text: P → Q is false only when P is true and Q is false. In all other cases, the conditional is true.

discovery.text: When P is false, P → Q is true regardless of Q. This is called a "vacuously true" conditional.

twist.text: This shocks beginners. "If 2+2=5 then I'm the Pope" is technically true in formal logic.

climax.text: The material conditional doesn't match everyday "if-then" perfectly, but it makes formal systems consistent.

quiz.question: When is P → Q false?
options: When P is true and Q is false
